quality_assessment: Page contains significant factual error about default case behavior. Otherwise well-structured with excellent diagrams and examples.

issues.description: Documentation incorrectly states that smart case is the default behavior
issues.current_content: By default, ripgrep uses **smart case**: if your pattern is all lowercase, the search is case-insensitive; if it contains any uppercase letters, the search becomes case-sensitive.
issues.should_be: By default, ripgrep uses **case-sensitive** matching. Use the -S/--smart-case flag to enable smart case behavior, where lowercase patterns are searched case-insensitively and patterns with uppercase are searched case-sensitively.
issues.fix_suggestion: Update the case sensitivity section to correctly state that case-sensitive is the default, and that smart case requires the -S flag. Update the diagram and tip box accordingly.
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/defs.rs:678-680, crates/core/flags/defs.rs:3190-3193 - all tests confirm CaseMode::Sensitive is default. The -s/--case-sensitive flag help text says 'Search case sensitively (default).'

issues.description: The tip box and diagram present smart case as the default behavior
issues.current_content:
!!! tip "Smart Case Default Behavior"
    Ripgrep's smart case is usually what you want: `rg error` finds all variations
issues.should_be: The tip should clarify that smart case is not the default but is often useful: 'Enable smart case with -S when you want lowercase patterns to match any case variation'
issues.fix_suggestion: Revise the tip box to say 'Smart Case is Useful' rather than 'Smart Case Default Behavior'. Update to explain when to enable it with -S.
issues.source_reference: Practical testing shows: `echo -e 'Error\nerror\nERROR' | rg error` only matches 'error', not all variations

issues.description: Flowchart suggests smart case is applied automatically without flag
issues.current_content: Flowchart shows pattern case automatically determining search behavior
issues.should_be: Either add a decision node showing 'Using -S flag?' before the case detection, or move this diagram to the -S flag explanation to make it clear this is opt-in behavior
issues.fix_suggestion: Restructure the section: (1) Explain default case-sensitive behavior first, (2) Then explain -S/--smart-case as an option with its flowchart, (3) Then cover -i and -s for explicit override
issues.source_reference: Default behavior requires explicit -S flag to enable smart case logic

issues.description: Documentation presents flags in order that doesn't match usage patterns (smart-case flag comes last despite being discussed first)
issues.should_be: Flags should be ordered: default behavior (no flag), -S (smart-case), -i (always ignore case), -s (always case-sensitive)
issues.fix_suggestion: Reorganize to: 1) Default behavior (case-sensitive), 2) -S/--smart-case for adaptive behavior, 3) -i for always case-insensitive, 4) -s for explicitly case-sensitive when overriding config
issues.source_reference: Logical progression from default → common option → explicit overrides
